newsitem.title: INDIA: India says amends export-import policy.
newsitem.headline: India says amends export-import policy.

text.p: The Indian Commerce Ministry said on Thursday that it had amended the nation's export-import policy to ease restrictions on some imports and encourage exports.

The ministry said in a statement that Export Promotion Capital Goods (EPCG) licences issued between 1992 and 1997, when the concessional rate of duty was 15 percent, would now be entitled to import capital goods at the new rate of 10 percent.
The lower rate, available under the export-import (Exim) policy for 1997-2002, will be available for goods yet to be cleared from customs against such licences.
It said the threshold limit for the purpose of recognition as an Export House, Trading House, Star Trading House or Super Star Trading House had been reduced.
The revised threshold on the Free-on-Board value of exports is 25 percent higher than the threshold limit during 1996/97 (April-March), it said.

The revised threshold limit on the net foreign exchange value of exports is equivalent to 80 percent of the revised threshold limit on the FOB value of exports, it said. The revised limit will be available for one year.

Exporters who were recognised as Export House, Trading House, Star Trading House or Super Star Trading House in 1996/97 and obtain recognition or renewal in 1997/98 have been given the option to claim special import licences (SIL) based on exports during the preceding licensing year, it said.
